{
  "contract": "Any surface that renders the Booker must treat the visitor's (booker's) selected time zone as a first-class input to the available-slots request: because an event type may carry a restriction schedule that is evaluated in the booker's zone rather than the host's, the set of slots the server returns is a function of that zone, so the zone must appear both in the request payload and in the client-side cache/refetch key of every slots query, and every layer that assembles or memoises that request must re-run when the zone changes. Any hook, wrapper or range-computation that derives the slots request while omitting the booker time zone from its dependency/cache identity breaks this contract, because a zone change then leaves a stale, differently-restricted slot set on screen until the query identity happens to change on a full reload.",
  "defect_location": {
    "repo": "calcom/cal.com",
    "summary": "The slots request is assembled on two parallel client paths and neither carries the booker time zone into the query identity. (1) Web app: apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useEvent.ts:L61-L105 defines useScheduleForEvent(), which reads the booker's zone via useBookerTime() (apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useEvent.ts:L96, implemented at packages/features/bookings/Booker/hooks/useBookerTime.ts:L6-L9 over useBookerStoreContext/useTimePreferences) and then calls useSchedule() at apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useEvent.ts:L105. useSchedule (apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useSchedule.ts:L53-L169) builds the request from the month range returned by useTimesForSchedule() (called at apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useSchedule.ts:L72; hook at packages/features/schedules/hooks/useTimesForSchedule.ts:L87-L96, whose args type UseScheduleWithCacheArgs is declared at L9 and duplicated at apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useSchedule.ts:L15) and dispatches it through useApiV2AvailableSlots() at apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useSchedule.ts:L147. useApiV2AvailableSlots (apps/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useApiV2AvailableSlots.ts:L11-L13) is a hand-rolled react-query hook with its own QUERY_KEY constant at L11 rather than a tRPC-derived key, so its cache identity is composed by hand and the booker zone is not part of it; a zone change therefore hits the same cache entry and no refetch is issued. (2) Platform/embeddable Booker: packages/platform/atoms/hooks/useAvailableSlots.ts has the identical shape — QUERY_KEY at L13 and useAvailableSlots() at L15 building its own queryKey around GetAvailableSlotsInput_2024_04_15 (packages/platform/types/slots/slots-2024-04-15/inputs/index.ts:L43) — and it is the slots source for packages/platform/atoms/booker/BookerPlatformWrapper.tsx (imported at L36, wrapper component at L50-L594, which itself knows the zone via useTimePreferences imported at L14 and computes the range via useTimesForSchedule imported at L17) and for packages/platform/atoms/calendar-view/EventTypeCalendarViewComponent.tsx (useAvailableSlots at L25, useTimesForSchedule at L15, useTimePreferences at L12). BookerPlatformWrapper is what packages/platform/atoms/booker-embed/BookerEmbed.tsx:L1 re-exports as the drop-in widget, which is why the same stale-slots symptom appears on both the first-party booking page and the embeddable booker. The zone itself is mutated from the booker UI (apps/web/modules/bookings/components/EventMeta.tsx:L101-L103 uses useBookerTime/useTimePreferences/useBookerStoreContext) and stored in packages/features/bookings/lib/timePreferences.ts:L7-L34, so the store update is reactive; what is missing is its propagation into the slots request identity in the hooks listed above.",
